title: AnimateDiff: Animate Your Personalized Text-to-Image Diffusion Models without Specific Tuning
layout_note: A module row above a bow-tie-shaped U-Net, joined by vertical drop-in arrows; the denoising flow runs left to right through the bow-tie with a return loop beneath.
grouping: Two layers on top of each other: above, a row of free-standing vertical columns titled 'Motion Modules of AnimateDiff' in bold; below, a large peach bow-tie (wide at both ends, pinched in the middle) standing for the image network, filled with orange-outlined vertical columns of decreasing then increasing height. Dashed arrows drop each motion column into the bow-tie next to its image column, under a grey band labelled 'Module Insert'. A text arrow 'Training Pipeline' points at the motion row from the left. A single legend entry (orange outlined box) at the bottom names the image layers.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded columns: image layers are orange outlines on the peach fill; motion modules are light-blue fill with a dark-blue outline and a green cap at the top. A noisy frame stack z_t at the left and a cleaner stack z_{t-1} at the right sit outside the bow-tie's ends; a grey dashed curved arrow 'Iterative Denoise' loops under the bow-tie from right back to left.
proposed_highlight: The proposed modules are the only blue-and-green objects and are first drawn outside the network, then shown inserted: the drop-in arrows make 'add to an existing model' the visual message.
lesson: Show plug-in temporal modules as a separate row of columns above the image network, dropped in by dashed arrows beside each matching image layer of a tinted bow-tie U-Net, with noisy and cleaner frame stacks at the two ends and a dashed loop for the sampling iterations.
notes: Venue ICLR 2024 read on the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024'). Figure 3 of this paper already has a card in the user layer, so Figure 2 (inference pipeline) was carded here.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: text-to-video by inserting motion modules into personalised T2I models

insights.structure: A peach hourglass silhouette stands for the frozen T2I U-Net with orange-outlined image-layer bars inside it, while a row of tall blue-green motion-module bars hangs above it and drops into the U-Net by dashed arrows through a 'Module Insert' label.
insights.data: Noisy latent frames z_t (stacked noisy squirrel images) sit at left and cleaner frames z_{t-1} at right, drawn as real image stacks; layers are drawn as thin vertical bars whose height echoes U-Net depth.
insights.emphasis: The motion modules are the only blue/green elements and appear twice (free above, inserted below), so the eye tracks the plug-in; the frozen network is muted peach with orange outlines.
insights.flow: Top-down for the insertion (Training Pipeline arrow -> motion modules -> dashed down arrows), left-to-right for denoising, with a grey dashed elliptical 'Iterative Denoise' loop around the U-Net base.
insights.avoid: The orange-outline legend at the bottom is the only key for image layers and the U-Net hourglass is unlabelled, so the frozen-vs-trained split relies on colour alone.

arrangement.units: one hourglass silhouette holding thin bar-shaped layers; motion modules as free bars above
arrangement.inputs_as: stack of noisy video frames z_t
arrangement.shared: the personalised T2I U-Net is shared and frozen
